sections.title: Outlook
sections.body: Vol easing is the day's continuing signal: VIXCLS shed more than a point back to a mid-teens handle while the index levels sat pinned, which reads as compression into next week's events rather than a directional bid — watch whether it holds below 16.34. Rates and credit strengthen the same read by not moving: DGS10 unchanged and HY OAS effectively flat mean nothing in the balance-sheet channel is repricing. What contradicts the calm surface is single-name dispersion beneath it — Semi-Cap/EDA and Cybersecurity bleeding double digits versus SPY while Devices/Endpoint and the ag basket lead — a rotation, not a broad de-risk. The front-end holds a 60% September hike, which keeps policy a live risk under all of it. First observable tomorrow: whether vol resumes lower or turns back up.

oneThing.title: The one thing
oneThing.body: Yesterday: no prior checks. This is the first note on file, so there is nothing to soften — the tape ranks as persistence with vol at the top. VIXCLS at 15.2 versus 16.34, a -1.14 pt move, is the widest displacement of any channel handed to me, and nothing disputes it: DGS10 unchanged, credit +1 bp. A falling VIX with rates and index pinned is compression, not direction — air coming out of hedges into next week's ADBE and ORCL prints and the 9/16 FOMC.
